approach: The only input is a one-paragraph calendar rules file. I restated its facts in a structured layout and did not invent the iteration or release train dates it lacks. This attempt removes the reference to a named role as the owner of the open items, because no input names one. The gaps are non-blocking open questions with no addressee. I didn't use connectors or the verifier, because the output is a few facts taken straight from the input.

judge.notes:
I checked every statement in the output against the input file at agents/hobasa-scheduler-agent/inputs/ITER-2026-10/SCH-P01/org.calendar_rules.md (commit 9404ef3), the step brief and the trigger. All of them are supported:
- Source line, the commit 9404ef3 and the trigger date 2026-10-25: in the input header (line 4) and the trigger.
- System demo on 24 October 2026 at 15:00: input line 7.
- PROD window 11:00-12:00 on the day after the demo, 25 October 2026: input line 10. This also matches the workbook action (11 am–12 pm, day after system demo).
- Timezone Asia/Kolkata: input line 13.
- Holidays "None in the window": input line 16.
- The "Not recorded" list (iteration start and end dates, release train dates): input lines 19-20.
- The new closing sentence ("These two items are not in the source file, so they are left blank rather than guessed."): true, because the input lists both items as not recorded.

The previous refusal point is fixed: the invented RTE addressee has been removed. No new names, numbers or dates have been added.

Weaknesses:
1. Incomplete against the workbook action. The action asks for iteration dates and release train dates. Neither is recorded, so the outcome "Approved calendar rules" is only partly achieved.
2. Unknowns are no longer marked as open questions. CLAUDE.md says to state an assumption and list it as a non-blocking open question. The earlier wording at least flagged a follow-up. The output file now has no open-question marker, so the gap shows only if the structured result lists these as open questions, which I could not check.
3. Almost no added value. The output copies the input word for word apart from the last sentence. The agent did not try the approved api:github connector or memory_search to find iteration or release train dates.
4. "None in the window" does not say which window: the PROD window or the iteration.
5. I could not compare against the git working-tree diff because a hook blocks shell commands for this step. All checks were made with Read on the two files.
